version.value: Complete first movement, including the first-movement cadenza
version.note: Commons describes the file only as the 1st movement; the performing edition and revision (Grieg revised the concerto repeatedly from 1872 to 1906–07) are not identified.

performers.note: Named in the Commons file description. Individual orchestral players are not identified.

date.note: The Commons date field is “?”. The repository describes Pandora Records as a label founded in 1973 that was active for over ten years, but the file carries no session date.

place.note: No venue is named. The repository describes its recordings as made in Seattle and credits Glenn White with some of them; the file itself does not say where this performance was recorded.

label.value: Pandora Music repository, ibiblio (Al Goldstein collection)
label.note: The repository says its master tapes, and LPs where tapes were missing, were archived by the Pandora Records project.

matrixTakeSides.note: The original tape or LP carrier is not identified.

credits.note: The repository acknowledges Glenn White for making and repairing some of its recordings; no engineer is credited for this file.

date.note: Neither the repository file nor the Commons page gives a digitisation date.

processing.value: Ogg Vorbis file hosted on Commons; MP3 access derivative generated by Commons
processing.note: No editing or noise processing by Contrapunctus; one complete source stream.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative of an Ogg Vorbis file; one source file, no concatenation or audio edits by Contrapunctus

composition.value: Public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms
composition.note: Grieg died on 4 September 1907. This says nothing about any modern edition.

recording.value: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 (the repository’s Open Audio License wording)
recording.note: The repository states that its files are available for free download subject to the EFF Open Audio License; Commons records this as CC BY-SA 2.0 and applies that licence to the file.
